title.zh: 宏记忆 · 插件市场（国内镜像）

description.en: Memory plugins for DeepSeek Harness: one unified surface, eight tools, one short standing injection.
description.zh: DeepSeek Harness 的记忆插件索引：一套统一工具面、一段最短常驻注入。 国内镜像：索引与代码走 gh-proxy 反代，逐字段与主索引相同，只有仓库地址带反代前缀。

description.en: One memory plugin instead of three: 8 unified memory_* tools and a single 1,235-character injection, with meow-memory's seven-layer SQLite as the main store and a rebuildable graph index. Tool schemas 56,759 B → 13,567 B (−76.1%), standing prompt 4,085 → 1,235 chars (−69.8%). Nothing was dropped: writes land in the main store first, graph links that cannot be written are queued instead of lost, and the setting page takes effect without a restart. 0.4.0 adds query decomposition, write-time consolidation, supersede + inflation checks, an entity layer on the graph, and co-occurrence query expansion learned from your own keywords — every one of them has an off switch and an on/off reading. 0.5.0 bridges CJK word forms so a paraphrase still lands. 0.6.0 makes scoring scale-adaptive: on a 660-entry snapshot, verbatim hit@1 0.895 → 0.921 and paraphrased 0.333 → 0.417 with zero wrong flips, and every hit now carries its `status`. 0.6.1 turns the three-trees-out-of-sync problem into one command (`tools/sync-trees.mjs`, dry-run by default, never deletes), pins the adaptive-idf wiring with two static regexes so a silent behaviour regression cannot pass green, and fixes a `%20` path bug in a maintenance script — engine bytes unchanged. 0.6.2 fixes a recall bug where the store said nothing when something was there: the noise floor dropped the only matchable word and left a word that does not exist in the store in its place (8 of 1,531 English questions came back empty). It now rescues only the words the noise floor dropped and never function words, so empty replies went 0.52% → 0 while hit@1/5/10/20, MRR and the 660-entry snapshot readings stayed bit-identical. 0.6.3 makes answers reproducible: a tie on score used to fall back to corpus order (V8's stable sort), so the same question could give two different top-tens depending on how the store happened to lay the rows out. The ladder now ends with updated-later-first and a natural id order, the adaptive-idf cluster pick no longer breaks ties by array index, and no ordering step uses localeCompare — and every reading stayed bit-identical. 0.6.4 fixes single-character queries: the tokenizer only emits CJK bigrams, so a one-hanzi question yields no tokens and the retrieval gate treated “cannot tokenize” as “not in memory” — the most direct questions (`读`, `钱`, `花`) always came back empty. It now falls back to a literal substring pass over title/content/keywords only when the query is a single CJK code point and tokenization produced nothing, still going through the same ordering ladder; English stopwords and punctuation stay closed. Every reading is bit-identical — this restores reachability, not ranking. 0.6.5 fixes punctuated single-character queries: the 0.6.4 gate demanded exactly one code point, yet a one-hanzi question almost always carries punctuation — `读？`, `钱。`, `花！`, `「读」` all came back empty. The gate now strips punctuation and whitespace first and requires exactly one remaining hanzi, allowing only punctuation/whitespace beside it; letters, digits and symbols stay closed, and a repeated character counts once. Every reading is bit-identical again — reachability, not ranking. 0.6.6 fixes dirty memories: `...d.keywords` in `docText` threw `TypeError: d.keywords is not iterable` for entries whose keywords were missing, null, or a comma-joined string (imported rows, rows written by other plugins, caller-built docs) — not one missing hit, but a whole failed search. Keywords now go through `kwList`: arrays, comma/ideographic-comma strings and JSON strings all count, and `docText`, the scoring fields `kwToks`/`kwSets`, `keywordHitScore` and the index signature all use it (comma-joined keywords finally reach tf-idf). Every reading is bit-identical — reachability again, not ranking. 0.6.7 fixes broken rows: a single null / undefined / scalar entry in `docs` (half-written rows, truncated imports, a caller passing ids instead of objects) made `docText` throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'title')`, and a non-array `docs` died on `docs.length`. Both entry points now pass a gate `liveDocs(docs)`: non-arrays return empty, entries are checked for object-ness, filtering happens only when something is broken, and a clean array is returned as the same reference (the index cache is keyed by a content signature, not identity, so nothing is invalidated); an all-broken array returns empty rather than scoring null as a memory. Every reading is bit-identical. 0.6.8 is about the lifetime of the checks themselves: versions, suite counts, assertion totals and time budgets all advance every release, so writing them as equality turns every bump into a false failure (`0.2.31→35` hit it four times; `0.6.2→0.6.7` hand-bumped `steps.length === 35 → 36` each time and edited two hand-copied doc numbers). Suite count is now a floor (`SUITE_FLOOR`: adding a suite needs no edit, losing one fails immediately), the current numbers in the docs are reconciled automatically against the baseline totals, historical milestones keep their own numbers, and the version ladder is compared by version, not layout. The engine is byte-identical; every reading is the same. 0.6.9 measures the ruler first: since 0.3.0 every published reading came from a single pass in a single order (corpus in storage order, questions in fixture order), and those single-pass numbers are exactly what rejected three candidates (English stemming, MMR, coverage re-rank). If the ruler is order-sensitive, those negatives carry the ruler own noise. `tools/probe-rigor.mjs` now pins seven properties: three consecutive passes give bit-identical readings (std = 0), reversed corpus order, three shuffles (seed 3/11/42), reversed question order, a second independent scorer, an injected same-score-corpus-order bias that must go red (A/B top-1 hits 23 to 15), and fixed tier sizes 45/14/10. On 69 real-corpus questions: hit@1 0.9565 / hit@3 0.9855 / MRR 0.9686, unchanged across passes and orders. The engine is byte-identical; LoCoMo and real-corpus readings are unchanged. 0.6.10 removes a fixed per-query cost: the search-index cache key is a content signature, and while the usual answer is that the store did not change, the price was paid in full every time. On four isomorphic corpora (660 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000) the signature consumed 28.8%-30.6% of a warm search (0.96 / 2.84 / 7.04 / 14.16 ms). It is now accounted per document: a WeakMap keyed by the doc holds a 32-bit per-doc hash plus a snapshot of the fields that feed it, compared by value (not object identity) before reuse; the per-doc hash had to be lifted out of the rolling value to be cacheable at all; shapes whose values cannot be compared fall back to direct computation. Signatures now cost 0.062 / 0.189 / 0.528 / 1.198 ms (15x, share down to 2.8%-3.5%) and a warm search 3.24 to 2.18, 9.67 to 6.80, 23.0 to 15.3, 49.2 to 37.6 ms. Ranking is byte-identical; LoCoMo and real-corpus readings are unchanged. 0.6.11 keeps paying down fixed cost: the remaining warm-search time is now accounted per channel, and the most expensive one is verbatim matching, which used to rebuild one lowercased string of the whole store on every query (id + project + title + content + keywords) just to answer whether an identifier appears verbatim, 2.03 MB at 10,000 docs and 35.7%-50.6% of a warm search; splitting that further showed 5.78 ms spent building strings against 0.51 ms of actual scanning. The haystack now lives in the index next to the token table, is built per document on demand and accounted (built / reused), and nothing is built when the query carries no identifier. The same change closed a 0.6.10 hole: the haystack contains project, project was never part of the signature, and once the string is cached a changed project would have been served from a stale index. Warm search: 2.04 to 1.62, 5.04 to 4.20, 11.88 to 9.12, 24.45 to 18.82 ms (-20.6% / -16.7% / -23.2% / -23.0%), verbatim share down to 18.6%-34.9%. Ranking is byte-identical; LoCoMo and real-corpus readings are unchanged. 0.6.12 keeps paying down fixed cost and targets the final ordering step. After the signature accounting of 0.6.10 and the verbatim accounting of 0.6.11, --cpu-prof attributed the largest remaining block to bandize (10,000 docs, 300 queries): to hand back the top ten it sorted the full hit list twice, once by _raw to assign bands and once by band, score, update time and id for the final order, while all three call sites only take the first k afterwards. Ordering was 40.3% of a warm search, about 11 ms per query, more than scanning documents. Band numbers are now written on the hit itself instead of a per-query Map, the comparator is factored into one orderOf ladder (band, then score, then more recently updated first, then natural id order) shared by both the full sort and the heap, and bandize takes a limit and selects the top k with a bounded max heap whose root is the worst selected hit; when the wanted count is not smaller than the total, the original full sort runs unchanged, so small stores and large k behave bit for bit as before. Bands and explain.band are only written on the surviving hits, and the temporary field is deleted. Search 27.377 to 19.985 ms (-27.0%), the production searchAdaptive path 31.086 to 23.097 ms (-25.7%), ordering share 40.3% to 21.5% (orderOf itself 0.9%), index reuse still 0.751 ms per query and cold index build unchanged at 270.7 ms. Ranking is bit-identical: the top k matches full-sort-then-slice across 500 random corpora and six k values, the total returned count stays 1,500, and LoCoMo plus the 52-question real-corpus readings are unchanged. 0.6.13 keeps paying down fixed cost and targets band assignment. After 0.6.12 capped ordering at the top k, a fresh --cpu-prof run (10,000 docs, 300 queries, 19.99 ms per search) showed the largest remaining block was still the full sort that exists only to assign bands: hits.slice().sort((a, b) => b[rawKey] - a[rawKey]) inside bandize, 21.5% of a warm search (bandize 10.9% plus the internal raw comparator 10.6%), paying comparator calls and object field reads for entries that can never reach the top k. Bands depend only on the distinct raw values after sorting, so the fix is three steps with identical semantics: copy raw values into a Float64Array and sort it with the native numeric sort (no comparator), walk it downward once to build a threshold chain (a0 is the maximum, a(i+1) is the largest value below 0.85 times a(i)), then binary-search each hit own value against the chain, where its band equals m minus 1 minus lo. Fallback: when any raw value is not a finite non-negative number (NaN, undefined, null, negative), the strictly decreasing anchor premise fails (0.85 times a negative value is larger, not smaller), so the whole pass falls back to the 0.6.13-era full sort setBandsBySort, and identified hits keep band minus one and stay out of the chain. Search 19.985 to 16.329 ms (-18.3%), the production searchAdaptive path 23.097 to 18.812 ms (-18.6%), band assignment share 21.5% to 7.8% (threshold chain 7.0% plus bandize 0.8%), index reuse still 0.703 ms per query, cold build 259 ms. Ranking is bit-identical: LoCoMo hit@1 0.3932, hit@5 0.6192, hit@10 0.6924, hit@20 0.7511, MRR 0.4958, recall@20 0.6322, zero empty answers, and the 52-question real-corpus readings match 0.6.12 exactly. 0.6.14 removes the leftovers from the hot path. After 0.6.13 cut band assignment from 21.5% to 7.8%, the function view only showed work being done (search self 45.8%, scanDoc 17.8%); a line-level attribution over cpuprofile positionTicks exposed the real cost: delete h._lv alone accounted for 791.5 ms, with delete h._vb and delete h._sr adding another 353 ms, so 1.14 s of a 5,671.8 ms sample went into removing values that had just been attached. The cause is four use-then-unset temporaries on each hit object (verbatim hit, pattern ratio, level intent, assertion density) that were cleaned up with delete, and delete pushes an object into dictionary mode, so every later property access, including the h._raw read inside the freshly optimized bandize, goes through a hash table; four saved assignments bought a slower whole path. Two changes keep semantics identical: the four temporaries move into parallel arrays indexed like hits (pushed right next to hits.push, read back by index), leaving the returned field set exactly as before; and idf is memoized per pass (within one pass idf is constant per term, so a per-query cache with idfAt yields bit-identical values without recomputing Math.log), with the cache reset when adaptive idf swaps its ruler. Two per-query allocations also disappear: raw.slice is only kept when explain is on, and the Math.max spread becomes a loop that preserves NaN propagation. Search 16.329 to 11.567 ms (-29.2%), or -57.7% against 27.377 ms in 0.6.12; the production searchAdaptive path 18.812 to 13.520 ms (-28.1%); zero delete calls left on the hot path, index reuse 0.679 ms per query, cold build 275 ms. Ranking is bit-identical: LoCoMo hit@1 0.3932, hit@5 0.6192, hit@10 0.6924, hit@20 0.7511, MRR 0.4958, recall@20 0.6322, zero empty answers, and the 52-question real-corpus readings match 0.6.13 exactly. 0.6.15 stops recomputing coverage per candidate. After 0.6.14 removed the 1.14 s of delete work, the function view again only showed work being done (search self 40.6%, scanDoc 18.8%); the line view named the cost: inside scanDoc the most expensive line was coverage, the loop that walks the query terms for every candidate and adds the idf of each term the document contains, at 573.9 ms over 300 queries, or 1.9 ms per query. The quantity itself is simple, the share of the query covered by a document, weighted by idf, but the algorithm was two-dimensional: for each candidate (up to 10,000) the full query vocabulary (dozens of terms) was asked again through a Map, hundreds of thousands of hash lookups per query just to produce 10,000 numbers, while the inverted index already records which documents each term appears in. Four changes keep semantics identical: per-query term idf is computed once into two Float64Arrays and read directly by the scoring loop; coverage is accumulated along the inverted index (a zero table sized by the document count, filled in the original query-term order, leaving one clamped division inside scanDoc), and because the addition order is unchanged every candidate keeps a bit-identical floating-point sum; when the inverted index is absent (explicitly disabled, or the query carries identifiers) the old per-candidate lookup path returns unchanged; and the candidate loop takes one record reference up front instead of re-resolving the same fields. The adaptive-idf ruler swap now re-accumulates both accounts in a fixed order: clear the idf cache, refresh term weights, rebuild the coverage table, then rescan. Search 11.567 to 10.673 ms (-7.8%), or -61.0% against 27.377 ms in 0.6.12; the production searchAdaptive path 13.520 to 12.522 ms (-7.4%); the coverage line 573.9 to 14.9 ms and scanDoc self time 23.8% to 18.8%; index reuse 0.698 ms per query and cold build 271 ms are flat within noise. Ranking is bit-identical: LoCoMo hit@1 0.3932, hit@5 0.6192, hit@10 0.6924, hit@20 0.7511, MRR 0.4958, recall@20 0.6322, zero empty answers, and all 52 real-corpus questions keep their scores and the two rank swaps. 0.6.16 stops looking up the term table for every candidate. After 0.6.15 removed the 573.9 ms of coverage work, the function view again only showed work being done (search self 48.0 percent, sigDocOf 9.5 percent, banding 7.5 percent); the line view named the next cost: the scoring loop that asks a Map for each query term of each candidate, 535.3 ms over 300 queries, about 1.8 ms per query. The quantity is term frequency times rarity times whether the hit was in the title or the keywords, and the first two inputs are fixed at index time; the inverted index already records which documents each term appears in. Three changes keep semantics identical: the inverted value grows from a list of document indexes to three parallel lists (index, term frequency, field-hit bits), with frequency and bits pushed in the same document-loop order so they stay index-aligned, and field weights are never multiplied into the index because they are per-query options that callers can override, so only the hit bits are stored and the weight is applied on the hot path; scoring runs the other way round, first preparing per-candidate constants (coverage, the length-normalisation denominator, the coordination term) and then, in the original query-term order, letting each term touch only the documents that contain it, adding its saturated term score to the raw score, so every candidate receives its addends in the same order and keeps a bit-identical floating-point sum; the finishing pass then applies synonyms, the coordination term and the entity layer per candidate with the same arithmetic as before; and the per-candidate path is untouched, still serving the case where the inverted index is disabled or the query carries identifiers. Search 10.67 to 8.35 ms (-21.8 percent, or -69.5 percent against 27.38 ms in 0.6.12), the production searchAdaptive path 12.52 to 10.16 ms (-18.9 percent), profiler samples 4,143.7 to 3,295.9 ms (-20.5 percent) with scanDoc gone from the top 25, index reuse still 0.69 ms per query. One cost, paid once: cold build 269 to about 300 ms, roughly 11 percent more, because each term stores two extra lists. One bug worth recording: the candidate list was not cleared at function entry, so the adaptive ruler swap pushed every candidate a second time and the finishing pass applied its factors twice, visible as an unchanged per-candidate path next to a shifted adaptive path. Ranking is bit-identical: LoCoMo hit@1 0.3932, hit@5 0.6192, hit@10 0.6924, hit@20 0.7511, MRR 0.4958, recall@20 0.6322, zero empty replies, and the 52-query real-store snapshot keeps all three tiers plus its two rank swaps. 0.6.17 trims the hit object before hydrating it. After 0.6.16 moved scoring onto the inverted index, search self time fell from 48 to 9 percent, and the most expensive remaining lines were no longer algorithm work but the receipt object literal itself: the scan loop built a fourteen-field hit for every candidate (level, title, content, importance plus five optional pass-through fields, with four conditional spreads), 134 to 176 ms per line and about 1.07 s over 300 queries, two thirds of the self time, while banding and trimming keep only the top k, so the plugin paid a full object for each of the thousands of entries destined to be dropped. Three changes keep semantics identical: the scan phase carries only what banding needs (subject, raw, cover, id, updated_at and score) plus an internal index, since band assignment and ordering read nothing else; after truncation the surviving k entries are hydrated back to the full object in the original key order, taking the score already on the lean object, because identifier bonus, level intent, assertion density and status digest have already been applied to it and recomputing would lose them, and replacing array elements in place rather than building a new array so the trimmed and rescueAdded properties survive; the explain and keepBand paths keep the full literal, since the former patches the object in place and the latter must keep the band for fusion. Search 8.35 to 3.5 ms (-58 percent, or -87 percent against 27.38 ms in 0.6.12), searchAdaptive 10.16 to 4.5 ms (-54 percent), profiler samples 3,295.9 to 1,808.2 ms, index reuse still 0.69 ms per query, cold build unchanged at 288 to 301 ms. Ranking is bit-identical: LoCoMo hit@1 0.3932, hit@5 0.6192, hit@10 0.6924, hit@20 0.7511, MRR 0.4958, recall@20 0.6322, zero empty replies, and the 52-query real-store snapshot keeps all three tiers plus its two rank swaps. A new probe covers six checks: the lean path and the full path are byte-identical after dropping explain, key order included, the keepBand path matches after peeling internal fields, no internal fields leak while the array properties remain, optional fields are still omitted or passed through, and both paths agree on a large corpus. 0.6.18 drops Set from the candidate set. After 0.6.17 trimmed and hydrated hit objects, a hot search costs 3.49 ms, and the top functions are all per-query fixed costs over ten thousand entries, while the candidate set was still paying an avoidable price: the inverted-index path merged the entries hit by query terms and their co-occurrence expansions into a Set with two add rounds and iterated it, 137.4 ms or 7.6 percent per line, followed by the scoring function at 112.2 ms, all spent on hashing and iterator allocation, when the semantics need only two things: an index-to-seen lookup and first-seen ordering. Two changes, identical semantics: deduplication becomes a Uint8Array bitmap, with the two dedup sites reading if (candAt[di] === 0) { candAt[di] = 1; candList.push(di); }, one for query terms and one for expansions; the candidate table keeps first-seen order, and the scoring function loops by index, with length normalization, the coverage table, the candidate array and both null checks, first pass and rescaled pass, now testing the candidate table. The fallback is untouched: with the inverted index off or an identifier in the query the bitmap is null and the full scan runs. Bit-identical because first-seen order is exactly the insertion order of the set, the bitmap answers only seen-or-not, and push preserves order, so the candidate array layout, scan order, floating point addition order and receipt order are unchanged. Search 3.49 to 3.01 ms (-13.7 percent, or -89 percent against 27.377 ms in 0.6.12), searchAdaptive 4.568 to 4.54 ms, profiler samples 1,808.2 to 1,678.4 ms, and the candidate block left the top twenty. Ranking is bit-identical: LoCoMo hit@1 0.3932, hit@5 0.6192, hit@10 0.6924, hit@20 0.7511, MRR 0.4958, recall@20 0.6322, zero empty replies, and the 52-query real-store snapshot keeps all three tiers plus its two rank swaps. A new probe covers six checks: the seven source facts including that Set has left the candidate block, a 200-case comparison of bitmap union against set union, bit-identical results with the inverted index on and off, that the synonym expansion path is really exercised because the trimmed counter goes from undefined to one while order is unchanged and only scores differ, an empty query never yields NaN, and 300 entries times 30 queries stay bit-identical on both paths. Self-checked by 46 suites / 3,761 executable assertions in about 220 seconds.
description.zh: 一个记忆插件顶三个：8 个统一 memory_* 工具 + 一段 1,235 字符常驻注入，主库仍是 meow-memory 的七层 SQLite，星图退成可重建的索引。工具 schema 56,759 B → 13,567 B（−76.1%），常驻注入 4,085 → 1,235 字符（−69.8%）。能力一条没砍：写入先落主库，连不上星图的连线排队不丢，设置页改完即刻生效、不用重启。0.4.0 又加了查询分解、写入巩固、自动取代与通胀体检、实体层、以及从你自己的 keywords 学出来的共现扩词——每一件都有开关，也都有开/关对照读数；0.5.0 用 CJK 词形桥让换说法也能落地。0.6.0 让打分随库规模自适应：660 条快照上照抄 hit@1 0.895 → 0.921、换说法 0.333 → 0.417、误伤 0，每条命中顺带带 `status`。0.6.1 把「三棵树没同步」做成一条命令（`tools/sync-trees.mjs`，默认只体检、从不删除），用两条静态正则钉住自适应 idf 的接线点（判据全绿但行为回退这种沉默故障过不去），并修掉一个维护脚本的 `%20` 路径 bug——引擎字节未变。0.6.2 修的是一个把「有」说成「没有」的缺陷：噪声地板剔掉了唯一能命中的词、留下库里根本不存在（df=0）的词顶位，1,531 条英文问句里 8 条回执为空；处方只救被噪声地板剔掉的词（虚词一个都不救），空回 0.52% → 0，hit@1/5/10/20、MRR 与 660 条快照三档读数逐位不变。0.6.3 让答案是可复现的：分数并列时以前会退回语料顺序（V8 稳定排序），同一个问句能因为存储布局不同给出两套前十；定序梯子现在末尾是「更新得更晚的在前」+ id 自然序，自适应 idf 挑簇不再按数组下标破平，整条链上也没有 localeCompare——所有读数逐位不变。0.6.4 修的是「一个汉字也是问题」：分词只产二元组，一个汉字的问句切出来是空数组，检索的第一道门就把「切不出词」当成「没有」，于是 `读`/`钱`/`花` 这类最直白的问法永远空手。现在只在「切不出词 + 单个汉字」时按原文子串在标题、正文与关键词里找一次，仍走同一套定序；英文停用词与标点一个都不放行。所有读数逐位不变——修的是可达性，不是排序。0.6.5 修的是「标点也是人打的」：0.6.4 的单字兜底只认「正好一个码点」，可人问一个字的时候问号几乎从不缺席——`读？`、`钱。`、`花！`、`「读」` 一个都回不来。现在把标点与空白剥掉再数，剥完正好剩一个汉字才走兜底，汉字之外只许标点或空白；字母、数字、符号一律不放行，同一个字重复按一个算。所有读数又是一位没动——修的仍是可达性，不是排序。0.6.6 修的是「脏记忆不许把整次检索打成异常」：`docText` 里的 `...d.keywords` 遇上缺字段 / `null` / 逗号串（导入行、别的插件写的行、调用方自拼的 docs）会抛 `TypeError: d.keywords is not iterable`——不是少一条命中，是整次检索一个回执都拿不回来。现在 keywords 统一走 `kwList`：数组、逗号顿号串、JSON 串都认，`docText`、打分面的 `kwToks`/`kwSets`、`keywordHitScore` 与索引签名全走它（逗号串的关键词从此真进 tf-idf）。读数一位没动，修的是可达性。0.6.7 修的是「一条坏行不许把整次检索打成异常」：`docs` 里混进一条 `null` / `undefined` / 标量（半写的行、导入截断、调用方把 id 列表当 docs），`docText` 的 `d.title` 会抛 `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'title')`；`docs` 整个不是数组时死在 `docs.length`。现在两个入口都过闸 `liveDocs(docs)`：非数组回空、逐条问「是不是对象」、脏了才过滤，干净数组原样返回同一引用（索引缓存的键是内容签名，不靠身份，缓存不会被打掉）；全是坏行时回空，不把 `null` 当一条记忆打分。读数一位没动。0.6.8 治的是判据自己的寿命：版本号、支数、断言总数、耗时预算每版都在动，写成等值就每升一版必红一次（`0.2.31→35` 四遍版本等值、`0.6.2→0.6.7` 每版手工抬 `steps.length === 35 → 36` 并连带改两处手抄的「N 支 / M 条」）。现在支数是地板 `SUITE_FLOOR`（只许加不许减，减一支立刻红、加一支不必动判据），文档里「现在」的数由探针读基线合计自动对账，历史里程碑冻结自己那版的数字，版本阶梯按版本号比。引擎一个字节没动，读数逐位相同。0.6.9 先量了尺子：0.3.0
